Panthers vs Packers DraftKings Showdown Picks: Thursday Night Football NFL DFS Captains, Projections and Sim Plays

DraftKings Showdown · Thursday Night Football, October 29 · NFL Week 8 · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 29, 9:10 AM ET

Jordan Love has the highest SPAGS projection in the Panthers at Packers DraftKings Showdown: 18.0 points at $10,000 FLEX, 27.0 at captain for $15,000. Across 10,000 simulations Love holds 62% of the winning-lineup credit. The case against Love is his range, not his role: a simulated floor of 6.0 points at a $10,000 FLEX salary, in a game with a 47.5-point total.

Chuba Hubbard has the largest captain share: 14.9% of the simulated winning-lineup credit comes with Hubbard at captain. The model gives him 17.4 carries and 2.9 targets. Matthew Golden is the next captain in line, at 11.7%. The model gives him 7.5 targets on 31.7 routes.

Green Bay is a 3.5-point favorite, and the implied totals are 25.5 for the Packers and 22 for the Panthers.

Behind Love, Hubbard and Golden, the next projections are Bryce Young (17.0, $9,600), Tetairoa McMillan (15.1, $9,400) and Christian Watson (14.4, $9,800).

Every projection below is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 29, 9:10 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. Winning-lineup and captain credit come from 10,000 simulations of the Showdown contest, and tied winning entries share credit. A player's simulated floor is his 10th-percentile score and his ceiling is his 95th. Showdown lineups use one captain, who scores 1.5x at 1.5x salary, and five FLEX players.

TNF Showdown captain picks: who the sim wins with

Captain: Chuba Hubbard, CAR RB ($9,000 FLEX / $13,500 CPT)

Chuba Hubbard holds 14.9% of the simulated winning-lineup credit as a captain, more than any other player in this game. At captain he costs $13,500 and the 17.4-point SPAGS model projection becomes 26.1 with the 1.5x captain multiplier. The model gives him 17.4 carries and 2.9 targets. Across 10,000 simulations Hubbard averaged 17.5 points with a simulated floor of 6.7 and a ceiling of 35.3. He holds 59% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 14.9% as the captain and 43.9% in a FLEX spot.

Captain: Matthew Golden, GB WR ($8,400 FLEX / $12,600 CPT)

Matthew Golden holds 11.7% of the simulated winning-lineup credit as a captain. At captain he costs $12,600 and the 13.5-point SPAGS model projection becomes 20.3 with the 1.5x captain multiplier. The model gives him 7.5 targets on 31.7 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Golden averaged 13.4 points with a simulated floor of 1.3 and a ceiling of 38.7. He holds 37% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 11.7% as the captain and 24.9% in a FLEX spot.

Captain: Tetairoa McMillan, CAR WR ($9,400 FLEX / $14,100 CPT)

Tetairoa McMillan holds 11.7% of the simulated winning-lineup credit as a captain. At captain he costs $14,100 and the 15.1-point SPAGS model projection becomes 22.7 with the 1.5x captain multiplier. The model gives him 7.8 targets on 34.4 routes. Across 10,000 simulations McMillan averaged 15.0 points with a simulated floor of 2.4 and a ceiling of 38.9. He holds 41% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 11.7% as the captain and 29.1% in a FLEX spot.

Build around Matthew Golden at captain with Jordan Love, Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan at FLEX. That is the core of the lineup that won the most simulations in Chris Spags' pool (8 of 10,000 simulated contests), and it leaves $9,000 for the last two FLEX spots.

Jordan Love leads the SPAGS model at 18.0 DraftKings points for $10,000 at FLEX, or 27.0 points at captain for $15,000.

Jordan Love is the most expensive player at $10,000 FLEX and $15,000 at captain. All 30 players with a SPAGS projection are listed above with FLEX salary, captain salary and projection.

At $5,000 and under, the best projected points per $1,000 belong to Trey Smack (9.3 points at $5,000), MarShawn Lloyd (6.8 points at $3,800) and Ryan Fitzgerald (8.1 points at $4,800).

The Packers are a 3.5-point favorite in a game totaled at 47.5, with implied team totals of 25.5 for the Packers and 22 for the Panthers.
